text:
Maya (CS): heads-up — Verge reported a major drop in citation grounding and recall after our 03:12 UTC rollout. Customer says results used to include exact doc links; now answers are vague or cite wrong pages.

Maya (CS): they pasted two queries and the top-3 citations for each. looks like reranker deprioritized the previously top doc. they say recall went from ~92% -> ~56% on their eval prompts.

Maya (CS): customer asked if we changed any index/embedding logic during the release. they saw a small spike in 429s during the canary but nothing severe.

deploy-bot: deploy v2-reranker (revision: rf3a) promoted to prod @ 2026-03-16T03:12:04Z by @jenna_prod :rocket:

Anika (ML Eng): thanks, grabbing the sample queries & results. can you paste the exact request payload + headers (model id, reranker config, embedding model) from their report?

Maya (CS): pasted —

Maya (CS): ```json
{
  "query": "best practices for PCI token rotation",
  "top_k": 10,
  "retrieval": {"index":"verge-main-v1","embedding_model":"openembed-v2"},
  "reranker": {"model":"rf3a","temperature":0.0}
}
```

Maya (CS): they also attached two PDFs that used to show up top.

Anika (ML Eng): initial checks — rf3a is the new reranker we rolled. embedding model unchanged. possible causes: reranker weights/regression, index reindex with different metadata, or a change in candidate generation.

Javier (Infra): logs show a small reindex job last night on verge-main-v1 at 02:45 UTC (auto compaction). no failures, but there was an index shard migration across regions.

Bryan (SRE): I can pull request traces for the requests around 03:10–03:20. can we get customer request IDs?

Maya (CS): provided customer request_id list: ["req_77a1","req_77a2"]. they can repro consistently on their side.

Anika (ML Eng): repro plan: 1) repro locally with their payload against rf2b (previous reranker) vs rf3a; 2) compare candidate sets from retrieval stage; 3) check embedding similarity scores and reranker logits.

Anika (ML Eng): quick hypothesis: rf3a has a different length-bias or anchor-feature weight causing longer PDFs to be deprioritized. will run A/B within dev infra.

Javier (Infra): while you do that, I'm checking the index commit history & metadata for verge-main-v1. if the compaction stripped section headings or altered doc titles, that could explain lost grounding.

Maya (CS): customer is asking for ETA and whether we can rollback. they are considering a temporary mitigation on their side but want us to revert if needed.

Bryan (SRE): if we confirm regression attributable to rf3a, we can rollback the reranker model at the routing layer quickly. need 2 approvals.

Anika (ML Eng): initial dev-run results: candidate generator unchanged, embedding distances roughly same, but reranker scores for the true-positive docs dropped by 3.4x on avg with rf3a. looks like a score-scaling mismatch (normalization bug?).

Anika (ML Eng): pushing a quick patch to rf3a normalization and re-evaluating.

Maya (CS): customer update sent: "Thanks — please keep us posted. This impacts critical compliance search."

Javier (Infra): confirmed index metadata intact post-compaction. no metadata loss.

deploy-bot: rollback request for model rf3a received by @Anika.

Bryan (SRE): coordinated rollback window at 03:48 UTC if patch doesn't verify. I'll prep runbook and hotspot channel.

Anika (ML Eng): patch verified on dev: normalized logits align with rf2b behavior on their eval set. scheduling canary test now for 1% traffic.

Maya (CS): will relay to Verge and ask them to validate on the canary slice.

Verge follow-up: customer confirmed canary results look back to normal for their tests.

Maya (CS): closing loop with customer and logging incident for postmortem. next steps: add unit test to catch normalization regressions, add a small retrieval/regression eval in CI with Verge's repro set, and document rollback playbook for model promotions.

Anika (ML Eng): filing PR with tests and postmortem notes.

Maya (CS): thanks team — great cross-func response. :white_check_mark:
